pages.transcription:
VIA AIR MAIL

ON BOARD
S. S. Argentina
14.8.40.

Dear Hanna and Manfred,
While in New York I had
one single letter from you, one
from the children and one from
Mama, and now it is again a
long time without news - but I
hope that everything is allright
with you, that Eva gets over safely
and in good company and that
she feels happy in her new home.
I am afraid my last letters from
Newyork were rather confused and
incoherent, it was a terrible rush
there last days as we worked with
Viertel every afternoon and sometimes
in the evening.
As to Salmons, I have written
that I had a good impression,
kind, friendly people who want
to have a child besides their own
boy of three. I have not seen
their home, but I had long
conversations with them and
feel sure that Eva will be
[...]

[Randnotiz rechts:] all dem, auch die Rein war herrlich
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Briefpapier der S.S. Argentina. Die linke Seite weist Textspuren auf, die durch das Papier scheinen (bleed-through), diese wurden gemäß Anweisung ignoriert. Die letzte Zeile des Haupttextes ist durch den Falz/Rand teilweise abgeschnitten.

pages.transcription:
in pleasant carefree surroundings
in good neighbourhood with a good
school and plenty of children
nearby. New Rochelle is a kind of
suburb of New York situated on
a lake, 40 minutes ride to New
York. Rose Wohl who knows them
will go and see Eva and pro-
mised to settle her elsewhere should
for some unforseen reason Eva not
be quite happy with those people.
I telegraphed you also to inform
Anita about Eva's arrival -
this was only to make quite sure
that Eva will be expected. There
is a very slight chance that Salmon's
might be away for a few days
and in this case Anita would
meet her and take her home. In
any case Anita and Salmon's will
communicate before Eva's arrival
which, I hope, will be very soon.
Either Salmon or Anita will cable
you immediately on Eva's arrival,
and I asked Anita to cable me
too. - I hope that I have prearranged
for any possibility, I have done my
best, but things were complicated
by the fact that people in Newyork have

VIA AIR MAIL

S. S. Argentina

only small apartments, that most people
- except our refugee friends - were away
and that all the schools which I
might otherwise have inspected were
closed for the summer. But the
arrangement as it is now should in
our opinion work out well and
Eva be happy there. Of course
it will be hard for her to travel by
herself and to be met by strangers
on arrival. I am terribly sorry
that we had to leave but there
were a number of reasons why we
could not stay any longer in New
York.
As to Heiner, I have written
to Mr. Berner, Rose's brother-in-law
and asked him for an affidavit.
Unfortunately your cable arrived
at a moment where also the last
Americans of our acquaintance had
left New York and so we could not
arrange anything for him. Also Mr.
Berner is away until the end of
the month, but I feel sure that

he will do it if he possibly can.
I have asked him to answer me
by air mail to Rio and I would
then cable you to inform him
about the dates and names so
that he can fill out the affidavit.
Of all the persons we know Mr.
Berner seemed the most likely to
do it. As to Ursel I did not try
anything as in her case the Bri-
tish re-entry permit would be
required should she not come in
under the quota. And I heard
from people trying in similar
cases without success.
I hope to find long letters
in Rio - you did not say anything
about yourself and Manfred's work.
Is Alice still with Horngrads? Did I
understand right that Marta could
stay, what will you do with Ursel
when Eva is gone, can you leave
her in Bath with the people who
moved in, and will you go back
to London then? Do just as you feel
it best for your own sake, don't
think of our house, it is more important
that the arrangements are suitable for you.

pages.notes: Farbskala und Grauskala zur Archivierung. Darunter ist ein Ausschnitt des Brieftextes (Seite 4) zu sehen, der hier nicht erneut transkribiert wird.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, die Handschrift ist klar. Die wenigen unsicheren Stellen betreffen lediglich den Randbereich des Papiers.
